name: DWC Requests
problem: Maintainers have limited bandwidth. Work beyond them comes from volunteers.
More volunteers want to help than we can walk through what they could do and what would be useful.
Volunteers tend to be junior. Their changes need oversight, and each yes or no gets explained one by one in chat.
Meaningful changes span front end and back end, but issues are tracked on separate boards for each project.
Requests have to go into GitLab, which already takes a technical person. Some of the best ideas come from non-technical people.
outcome: Work we haven't approved never starts. A volunteer can propose work, or claim work we've approved, and nothing else.

reqs.text: Work that has not been approved never starts
reqs.why: Approval must gate work. The board shows self-approval as a problem in A; no story shows enforcement in B–D, so that stays open.
reqs.chk: Try to start work and open an MR without approval, including approving your own request. It must be blocked.

reqs.text: A non-technical person can send an idea
reqs.why: GitLab intake takes a technical person; D adds a request form and SSO.
reqs.chk: Have a non-technical contributor submit an idea and answer a follow-up without using GitLab.

reqs.text: Maintainers can ask, decide and explain
reqs.why: Maintainer bandwidth is limited, and each yes or no should be explained in the workflow.
reqs.chk: Ask a follow-up, accept an answer, and decline with a reason the requester can see.

reqs.text: Front-end and back-end work followed together
reqs.why: Changes span both codebases; D shows App and BackEnd MRs linked to one item.
reqs.chk: Link two MRs from separate projects to one approved item and follow them to done together.

reqs.why: The boundary allows claiming approved work, not starting unapproved work.
reqs.chk: Approve a request, claim its work item, and confirm another volunteer sees it as taken.

reqs.text: Requesters can find status, reasons and answers
reqs.why: Requesters should not have to repeat the conversation in chat.
reqs.chk: Ask for information, receive an answer, change status, and confirm the requester sees why.

reqs.why: Rate each shape against the appetite you set.
reqs.chk: Estimate each shape's build against the appetite and cut line.
